title: Stoichiometry
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Stoichiometry.

concepts.def: The sum of the relative atomic masses of all the atoms shown in a compound's formula.
The unit of amount of substance; one mole contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles and has a mass equal to the Mr in grams.
The coefficients in a balanced equation give the ratio of moles of each substance that reacts and forms.
The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound, calculated from reacting masses or percentages.
One mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³ at room temperature and pressure.
The reactant that is completely used up first; it determines the maximum amount of product that can form.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Stoichiometry — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Stoichiometry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Stoichiometry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The relative formula mass of CO₂ (C = 12, O = 16) is:
How many moles are in 9.0 g of water (Mr = 18)?
options: 0.50 mol
2.0 mol
0.20 mol
9.0 mol

mcqs.q: In 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, how many moles of O₂ react with 4 mol of H₂?
options: 2 mol
4 mol
8 mol
1 mol

mcqs.q: The volume of 0.50 mol of any gas at room temperature and pressure is:
options: 12 dm³
24 dm³
48 dm³
6 dm³

mcqs.q: Does a bigger coefficient in an equation mean a bigger mass of that substance?
options: No — coefficients give mole ratios; to compare masses you must multiply moles by each substance's Mr.
Coefficients show the temperature each substance must reach.
2H₂ must weigh more than O₂ in 2H₂ + O₂ because its number is bigger.
Mass always increases during a reaction because energy is added.

mcqs.q: Is mass lost when a reaction gives off a gas?
options: Mass is destroyed in fizzing reactions because the flask ends up lighter.
No — mass is conserved; the escaping gas carries its mass away, so all products together still equal the reactants.
Mass always increases during a reaction because energy is added.
Coefficients show the temperature each substance must reach.

mcqs.q: Do equal masses of two different gases contain equal numbers of molecules?
options: One gram of any gas always contains the same number of molecules.
Coefficients show the temperature each substance must reach.
No — equal volumes at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers; equal masses only match if the Mr values are the same.
Heavier gases always contain more molecules per gram.
